# Exercise stream_tar with and without an index, on bytes and stream receivers.
base64 small.base64 small.tar
base64 small_gz.base64 small.tar.gz
base64 nested.base64 nested.tar
base64 sparse.base64 sparse.tar

mito -use file,mime,stream,lines,try src.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want.txt

-- src.cel --
{
	// Indexes count only regular files: the directory, symbolic link and
	// hard link in the archive are skipped.
	"index_0":   file('small.tar').stream_tar(0).decode_lines().map(x, x),
	"index_1":   file('small.tar').stream_tar(1).decode_lines().map(x, x),
	"all":       file('small.tar').stream_tar().decode_lines().map(x, x),
	"range":     try(file('small.tar').stream_tar(2)),
	"negative":  try(file('small.tar').stream_tar(-1)),
	"not_tar":   try(b"this is not a tar archive".stream_tar(0)),

	// Stream receivers.
	"stream_index": file('small.tar.gz').stream_gzip().stream_tar(1).decode_lines().map(x, x),
	"stream_all":   file('small.tar.gz').stream_gzip().stream_tar().decode_lines().map(x, x),

	// stream_gzip on a stream: a gzip file inside a tar archive.
	"gzip_in_tar_index": file('nested.tar').stream_tar(0).stream_gzip().decode_lines().map(x, x),
	"gzip_in_tar_all":   file('nested.tar').stream_tar().stream_gzip().decode_lines().map(x, x),

	// GNU sparse files are regular files, so they are counted and joined.
	// Line sizes are shown since the hole is 8189 NUL bytes.
	"sparse_types": file('sparse.tar', 'application/x-tar').File.map(f, [f.Name, f.Type, size(f.Data)]),
	"sparse_index": file('sparse.tar').stream_tar(1).decode_lines().map(x, size(x)),
	"sparse_all":   file('sparse.tar').stream_tar().decode_lines().map(x, size(x)),
}
-- small.base64 --
